title: Translate and beat · Level 3: A rosette
brief: The class robot starts in the middle of a 2400 x 2400 mm floor facing +x (starts vary 10 mm and 2 degrees); the level fixes the robot. A rosette: 8 regular hexagons of 200 mm sides, each turned 45 degrees from the last, ending back on the start. The closing error is the distance from the start to the end, plus 2 mm per degree. The run ends when the program ends, or at 120 s. Line budget: 11 non-blank lines (fewer than the 12 of the G4.1 blocks reference). 50 points for a closing error under 30 mm, plus 40 x min(1, 5 mm / error), plus 10 at or under par time with the program within the line budget. A run that does not draw every side (the axle's middle travels 90 % of the perimeters and each shape encloses 80 % of its area) scores 0. Pass: mean 60 or more over 5 runs, 4 of them closing within 30 mm (every side drawn). Par: 70 s.

score.run: if(trailLength >= 0.9 * perim & pieceArea_1 >= 0.8 * area1, let e = (pieceClose_1 + headW * pieceTurn_1) in round(if(e < closeMm, 50, 0) + if(e <= precMm, 40, 40 * precMm / e) + if(time <= par & programLines <= lineBudget, 10, 0), 1), 0)

closes.value: count(r in runs: r.trailLength >= 0.9 * perim & r.pieceArea_1 >= 0.8 * area1 & (r.pieceClose_1 + headW * r.pieceTurn_1) <= closeMm)

sources.where: G5.1 Translate and beat, the challenge paragraph and the level table (level 3)
G4.1 Shape artist: every side drawn (90 % of the perimeter, 80 % of the area by the shoelace formula), a stop (still 0.9 s after first moving: 5 deg/s, 3 mm/s)
